words.meaning: Having or showing great knowledge from study; scholarly.
words.example: The erudite professor could discuss any topic from history to physics.

words.meaning: Tending to say very little; reserved in speech.
words.example: The taciturn farmer rarely spoke more than a few words at dinner.

words.meaning: Holding on firmly; not giving up easily.
words.example: The tenacious climber kept trying until she reached the summit.

words.meaning: Seeming to be everywhere at the same time; very common.
words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in almost every part of daily life.

words.meaning: Mocking in a scornful or sarcastic way.
words.example: He gave a sardonic smile when his rival tripped during the race.

words.meaning: Overly concerned with minor details or rules; showing off knowledge.
words.example: The pedantic editor corrected every tiny comma in the essay.

words.meaning: Using far more words than are needed; wordy.
words.example: The verbose report could have said the same thing in half the pages.

words.meaning: Courage and strength shown while facing pain or hardship.
words.example: She faced the long illness with remarkable fortitude.

words.meaning: Spreading harmfully in a gradual, often unnoticed way.
words.example: The insidious rumor slowly damaged her reputation before anyone noticed.

words.meaning: To make something unclear or difficult to understand on purpose.
words.example: The spokesperson tried to obfuscate the truth with confusing technical terms.

words.meaning: A very large, countless number of something.
words.example: The night sky revealed a myriad of stars above the campsite.

words.meaning: Calm and peaceful; not easily upset or excited.
words.example: The placid lake reflected the mountains perfectly on a windless morning.

words.meaning: Expressing opinions or feelings in a loud, forceful way.
words.example: The vociferous crowd booed loudly when the referee made the call.

words.meaning: Designed to impress others; showy in an obvious way.
words.example: He drove an ostentatious gold car just to attract attention.

words.meaning: Showing adult abilities or understanding at an unusually young age.
words.example: The precocious child was solving math problems years ahead of her grade.

words.meaning: To respond to an action or feeling by doing or feeling the same in return.
words.example: She helped him with his project, and he reciprocated by tutoring her in math.

words.meaning: Fearless and brave, especially when facing danger.
words.example: The intrepid explorer crossed the frozen glacier alone.

words.meaning: Likely to change suddenly and unpredictably, especially for the worse.
words.example: The stock market remained volatile throughout the entire week.

words.meaning: Sweet and smooth-sounding; pleasant to hear.
words.example: Her mellifluous voice made the lullaby even more soothing.

words.meaning: Lasting only for a short time; temporary.
words.example: The joy of winning the game was transient once he remembered his exam the next day.
